text:
elena: heads up — after the nightly image rebuild that bumped runtime base -> CUDA 12.1, three GPU nodes in us-west2 failed to bring up nvidia modules during boot. seeing modprobe errors and containers hitting NCCL init failures.
elena: sample from one node /var/log/kernel.log:```Feb 22 03:12:01 host kernel: nvidia: disagrees about version of symbol module_layout (expected 5.19.0, found 5.15.0)
Feb 22 03:12:01 host kernel: modprobe: FATAL: Module nvidia not found in directory /lib/modules/5.15.0-45-generic```
samir: ugh, sounds like the rebuild picked up a different kernel-headers target. we recently changed the builder image to use ubuntu:22.04 + custom installer that doesn't pin linux-headers. likely produced driver binaries for a different kernel ABI.
elena: confirmed uname -r shows 5.15.0-45 but the module dir contains 5.19 folders. ls /lib/modules shows mismatched dirs.
kai: @elena can you share the image digest and the CI job id that produced it? I'll check the builder logs.
elena: digest sha256:7f4b2e..., CI job: infra-image/7821. quick grep in CI logs shows apt installed linux-headers-generic but no explicit pin.
samir: we probably did a host-level kernel update on the node pool last week (auto-upgrade), and the new image builder pulled the newest headers in CI (5.19). when that image gets deployed to hosts still running 5.15, modules are incompatible.
nate: result in prod: kubelet tried to mount GPU devices into containers, container starts but ML service logs: "NCCL WARN: Unhandled system error (NVML failed to initialize)" and then OOMs as fallback threads spin. short-lived pods crashlooping.
infra-bot: node-gpu-uw2-17 drained automatically by autoscaler after 3 GPU-health failures. ticket created: INFRA-4921.
ops-oncall: rolling out a rollback ASAP. what's the quick rollback plan? revert to previous image tag?
samir: rollback to previous digest (sha256:1a2b3c...) is safest. but need to ensure CI doesn't re-publish the bad digest. block the pipeline.
kai: I've flagged CI job 7821 as failed and paused the nightly pipeline for image-builder. also adding an explicit linux-headers pin to the Dockerfile. will push PR in a minute.
elena: for immediate mitigation, we should cordon and drain remaining nodes that got the new image and redeploy workloads to nodes running the old image. also update nodepool autoscaling policy to avoid creating new nodes from the bad image.
samir: +1. I'm preparing a canary patch: update builder to pin headers to kernel version used in our base AMI, rebuild image and test on a 2-node canary pool in eu-west-1.
nate: timeline? we have about ~120 GPU-hours lost so far with retries and restarts. cost impact estimate ~ $1.8k for extra preemptibles churn. ops-oncall: include that in the incident note.
kai: PR: https://internal/redwood/infra-image/pulls/56 — adds "linux-headers-$(uname -r)" pin and a sanity check step: run `modprobe -n nvidia` inside a host-kernel-matching container.
elena: can someone run dkms status on the affected hosts to see if any dkms rebuilt drivers unexpectedly?
samir: ran it on two nodes: `dkms status` returns nothing (drivers installed from vendor packages in image), not DKMS-managed.
kai: I'm adding a CI gate that runs a quick `uname -r` vs `/lib/modules` directory match inside the image build. if mismatch -> fail.
elena: for recovery steps I'm doing now: 1) disable auto-upgrade for that nodepool, 2) roll back DaemonSet to previous node driver container image, 3) cordon bad nodes and trigger replace.
nate: I'll submit a cost recovery note and include the kube events. we should also notify customer-facing teams in case of SLA blips in us-west2.
ops-oncall: @samir @kai can you schedule a postmortem tomorrow? capture why headers weren't pinned, why our canary didn't catch it, and decide on a permanent policy for kernel-driver parity.
samir: already capturing logs and will add to INFRA-4921. initial notes: require host/kernel pinning in image + builder check + small canary (<=5 nodes) with explicit module load verification.
elena: small quick fix: for nodes still booting, `sudo apt-get install --reinstall nvidia-driver-525` plus reboot brought modules back on one node, but it's a risky manual step at scale. prefer immutable rollback.
kai: rolling canary now in eu-west-1, rebuilding image with pinned headers, will post results in ~30m. :thumbsup:
elena: thanks — holding any further CUDA12.1 pushes until canary passes. adding ops-oncall to incident channel. :boom:
